label: Geneva — UN Mediation Hub
sub: Headquarters of OHCHR, UNHCR, UNOG, and dozens of peace processes including Syria, Yemen, Libya consultations. Annual Human Rights Council sessions.

label: Oslo — Oslo Accords (1993)
sub: Secret back-channel talks hosted by Norway's FAFO Institute led to the Israel–PLO Declaration of Principles signed Sep 13, 1993. Norway continues as peace mediator in Colombia (ELN/FARC) and other contexts.

label: Doha — Peace Talks Hub
sub: Host of U.S.–Taliban Doha Agreement (Feb 2020), Gaza ceasefire negotiations (2023–26), Sudan peace consultations, and Afghan intra-dialogue. Qatar's mediation role is central to multiple active processes.

label: Belfast — Good Friday Agreement (1998)
sub: The Belfast Agreement of April 10, 1998 ended 30 years of 'The Troubles'. Northern Ireland's power-sharing institutions remain the model for consociational peace. Brexit tensions test the agreement's Irish dimension.

label: Dayton — Bosnia Peace Accords (1995)
sub: The General Framework Agreement for Peace in Bosnia was initialed at Wright-Patterson AFB on Nov 21, 1995, ending the Bosnian War. Created Bosnia's two-entity structure under a unified state. NATO IFOR/SFOR enforced peace.

label: Bogotá — Colombia FARC Peace (2016)
sub: Final peace agreement with FARC-EP signed Nov 24, 2016 after 4 years of Havana negotiations. JEP (Special Jurisdiction for Peace) operates here. Total Peace policy of Petro government includes ELN talks, now suspended 15+ months after January 2025 Catatumbo massacre.

label: Havana — Colombia Peace Talks Venue
sub: Cuba hosted FARC–government talks 2012–2016 and continues as guarantor for ELN negotiations under Petro's Total Peace framework. Joint guarantor with Norway. ELN talks suspended since January 2025 Catatumbo massacre.

label: Addis Ababa — African Union HQ
sub: African Union Commission headquarters. Hub for IGAD, AUHIP (Sudan), AU peace missions. Hosted Ethiopia–Tigray Pretoria Agreement (2022) implementation monitoring. Key venue for Horn of Africa peace diplomacy.

label: Nairobi — IGAD / EAC Peace Hub
sub: Hosted Sudan CPA signing (2005), South Sudan R-ARCSS follow-on talks, and DRC–Rwanda Nairobi Track negotiations. IGAD headquarters. Kenya's Uhuru Kenyatta mediated Ethiopia–Tigray Pretoria process. RSF's Hemeti in Apr 2026 Nairobi talks with UN envoy Haavisto.

label: Pretoria — Ethiopia–Tigray Agreement (2022)
sub: Cessation of Hostilities Agreement signed Nov 2, 2022, ending 2 years of devastating war. AU-mediated by Obasanjo, Kenyatta, Mlambo-Ngcuka. Most significant African peace deal of the 2020s.

label: Jeddah — Sudan Peace Platform
sub: U.S.–Saudi Arabia jointly host Jeddah talks between SAF and RSF since May 2023. Multiple ceasefire declarations signed here have collapsed within hours. US Adviser Boulos presented five-pillar peace roadmap on Sudan's 3-year anniversary, April 15, 2026.

label: Stockholm — Yemen Hodeidah Agreement (2018)
sub: UN-brokered Stockholm Agreement of Dec 13, 2018 includes Hodeidah port ceasefire and prisoner exchange framework. UN Mission to support the Hodeidah Agreement (UNMHA) monitors ceasefire. Prevented catastrophic battle for Yemen's main supply port.

label: Minsk — Ukraine–Russia (Minsk I & II)
sub: Minsk Protocol (Sep 2014) and Minsk II (Feb 2015) established ceasefire and political roadmap for Donbas. OSCE monitored compliance. Russia's 2022 full invasion rendered the Minsk framework defunct. Both parties dispute who negotiated in bad faith.

label: Kyiv — Russia–Ukraine: Ceasefire Expired; Istanbul Direct Talks Proposed
sub: Russia's Feb 24, 2022 invasion. The U.S.-brokered 72-hour ceasefire (May 9–11) expired May 11 without extension — Russia fired 200+ drones at Ukraine within hours of expiry. May 13: Zelensky publicly accepted direct talks with Putin in Istanbul (around May 15), marking a potential breakthrough after 3+ years of war. As of May 13, the Kremlin had not confirmed Putin's personal attendance — the breakthrough remains conditional. If confirmed, this would be the first Zelensky–Putin meeting since March 2022. Turkey (Erdogan) proposed as host. The 1,000-per-side POW exchange continues as the only ceasefire tangible output. Core gaps unbridged: Russia demands recognition of all four annexed oblasts; Ukraine refuses territorial concessions without NATO-equivalent security guarantees.

label: Gaza — Ceasefire Negotiations
sub: Qatar/Egypt/U.S.-mediated ceasefire negotiations since October 2023. Phase I framework agreed Jan 15, 2025 (42-day pause, hostage releases). Phase II permanent ceasefire disputed. Over 50,000 Palestinian deaths reported; 2M displaced within Gaza.

label: Khartoum — Sudan Civil War
sub: SAF vs RSF conflict erupted Apr 15, 2023. Three-year mark Apr 15, 2026: 150,000+ killed, 14M displaced, famine in Darfur. US imposes sanctions and presents five-pillar peace roadmap. SAF retook capital Mar 2025; RSF controls most of Darfur.

label: Goma — DRC M23/Rwanda Conflict
sub: M23 rebels captured Goma Jan 27, 2025. Washington Accords (Dec 2025) stalled: Rwanda non-compliant (US: 'deeply disappointing' Apr 23). Positive step: DRC National Assembly adopted ratification bills Apr 28 and sent to Senate for second reading — domestic legal commitment to the accords framework. COVM verification active; FDLR not disbanded; 7M+ displaced in eastern DRC.

label: Cotabato — Bangsamoro Peace (Philippines)
sub: Capital of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM), established 2019 under the Bangsamoro Organic Law. MILF decommissioning proceeds in phases. BIFF and Abu Sayyaf remain spoilers.

label: Freetown — Sierra Leone Post-Conflict TJ
sub: Special Court for Sierra Leone operated 2002–2013, convicting Charles Taylor (in absentia) and RUF leaders. Truth and Reconciliation Commission completed its work 2004. Sierra Leone recovery model cited as post-conflict success despite ongoing governance challenges.

label: Bogotá — Colombia JEP (Transitional Justice)
sub: Colombia's Special Jurisdiction for Peace (JEP) investigates war crimes by FARC and military. Macro-case 01 examines 6,402+ cases of 'false positives' (civilians killed by army and registered as combatants). Colombia's TJ model is the most advanced in the Americas.

label: Banda Aceh — Helsinki MOU (2005)
sub: Post-tsunami peace breakthrough: Helsinki MOU ended 29-year GAM insurgency. EU and ASEAN monitoring mission verified demobilization. Aceh given special autonomy and oil revenue sharing. Considered a landmark post-disaster peace opportunity.

label: Mogadishu — Somalia Reconciliation
sub: AU Mission in Somalia (AMISOM/ATMIS) and UN Assistance Mission (UNSOM) support federal reconciliation process. Clan-based power sharing (4.5 formula) underpins government formation. Al-Shabaab controls 20%+ of territory. National Consultative Council attempts to resolve federal-state disputes.

label: Tripoli — Libya Peace Process
sub: Government of National Unity (GNU) recognized by UN but contested by Benghazi-based government. Libya Political Dialogue Forum (LPDF) attempts to bridge east-west divide. Ceasefire signed Oct 2020 broadly holds but elections remain blocked since Dec 2021. Turkey and UAE/Egypt back competing factions.

label: Nicosia — Cyprus Reunification Talks
sub: UN-mediated talks on bizonal bicommunal federation have continued since 1974 Turkish intervention. Most recent formal talks at Crans-Montana 2017 collapsed. UN Special Adviser Jane Holl Lute conducts informal consultations. Divided capital remains last divided city in EU-candidate zone.

label: Kathmandu — Nepal Transitional Justice
sub: Nepal's Truth and Reconciliation Commission and Commission on Enforced Disappearances were established under the 2014 TRC Act but stalled repeatedly. A landmark Supreme Court ruling 2024 requires accountability for conflict-era crimes. Nepal's TJ process is one of the world's longest-stalled.

label: Islamabad — US–Iran MOU Back-Channel; India-Pakistan LoC
sub: Pakistan hosted Round 1 of US–Iran talks April 11–12 (collapsed); Round 2 aborted April 26. Iran submitted 14-point proposal May 2 (rejected). May 6: Project Freedom paused. May 10 — KEY DEVELOPMENT: Iran formally submitted its response to the US one-page MOU via Pakistan back-channel (Bloomberg/IRNA); contents undisclosed; US review underway. Framework: end to war declaration + 30-day negotiating window on Hormuz, nuclear limits, sanctions — missile program and proxy forces deferred. Iran insists on enrichment rights and UNSC-backed guarantees; Khamenei approval required. Pakistan also served as the diplomatic pivot during Operation Sindoor (May 2025); India-Pakistan LoC ceasefire 1-year anniversary May 10, 2026. Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner lead US team.

label: India–Pakistan LoC — Operation Sindoor Ceasefire (1-Year Anniversary)
sub: May 10, 2026: One-year anniversary of the India–Pakistan ceasefire that ended Operation Sindoor (May 7–10, 2025). India struck nine alleged terror camps in Pakistan/PoK following the April 22, 2025 Pahalgam attack (26 killed). Ceasefire announced by US Secretary Rubio; India describes it as bilateral. One year on: ceasefire holding but Indus Waters Treaty suspended, trade severed, diplomatic ties downgraded, both sides on high alert. No formal normalization or peace process framework established. Al Jazeera: 'rising risks and deepening instability' despite ceasefire. Trump nominated for Nobel Peace Prize by Pakistan for brokering the truce. No formal peace talks or confidence-building measures launched.

label: Washington DC — Lebanon-Israel Round 3 Talks Underway May 14–15
sub: U.S.-facilitated Washington Accords (DRC–Rwanda) signed December 4, 2025; 5th Joint Oversight Committee met April 23, 2026. Lebanon-Israel Round 1 (April 22–23, 2026) produced a 3-week ceasefire extension; Round 2 continued momentum. Round 3 — May 14–15, 2026 — underway at State Department: Israeli delegation led by Amb. Yechiel Leiter + IDF Brig.-Gen. Amichai Levin; Lebanese delegation led by Simon Karam + Amb. Nada Hamadeh Mouawad; US: Amb. Huckabee, Amb. Issa, Rubio adviser Needham, Secretary Rubio direct. US official: 'productive, positive.' Core impasse: Israel demands Hezbollah disarmament south of Litani as precondition for withdrawal; Lebanon demands unconditional IDF withdrawal first under 1701. CEASEFIRE EXPIRES MAY 17 — extension is the key deliverable. Hezbollah continues opposing the Washington direct format. May 14: 52 senators + 177 reps wrote to Trump opposing any Iran deal permitting enrichment, narrowing MOU diplomatic space.

label: Beirut — Ceasefire Expires May 17; Round 3 Washington Talks Underway
sub: US-brokered ceasefire began April 16, 2026. May 11: 51 killed in 24 hours (Israel bombed Beirut suburbs; Hezbollah 24 attacks). May 12: Hezbollah SG Qassem urged Lebanon to quit Washington direct talks, calling them 'concession to enemy.' May 13: Israeli strikes kill 12 in Lebanon on eve of Round 3 talks. May 14–15 — ROUND 3 UNDERWAY: US official characterizes talks as 'productive, positive.' Ceasefire framework EXPIRES MAY 17 — extension is the central deliverable. Fundamental impasse persists: Israel demands Hezbollah south-Litani disarmament before IDF withdrawal; Lebanon demands unconditional IDF withdrawal under 1701. If no extension, Lebanon risks return to active hostilities at a moment of severe domestic political crisis. Hezbollah maintains opposition to the Washington direct format — sustaining spoiler pressure on PM Salam and President Aoun.

label: Strait of Hormuz — MOU Deadlocked; Congress Opposes Enrichment Deal
sub: Critical maritime chokepoint — ~20% of global oil trade. Iran closed Strait March 2026; ~750 vessels trapped; $6B/month Iranian oil exports blocked; US gas $4.48/gal (highest since July 2022). May 12: Trump declared ceasefire 'on massive life support'; US imposed new sanctions on Iranian nuclear research and ballistic missile supply chains. May 13: Iranian parliament speakers (Ghalibaf, Rezaei) threatened 90% weapons-grade uranium enrichment if Iran is attacked. Iran holds 400–460 kg at 60% enrichment (upgradeable in 1–2 weeks). May 14 — DOMESTIC PRESSURE: 52 US senators + 177 representatives wrote to Trump opposing any deal permitting Iranian uranium enrichment — eliminating the 12-15 year compromise window Witkoff/Kushner had been exploring. Iran's red line: no surrender of enrichment rights. No new talks scheduled. MOU framework deadlocked across all dimensions. Trump in China — possible indirect Xi-Iran back-channel.

label: Cebu — 48th ASEAN Summit (May 5–9, 2026)
sub: The Philippines hosted the 48th ASEAN Summit in Cebu, May 5–9, 2026. Myanmar dominated regional diplomacy — five years after the Five-Point Consensus, ASEAN agreed only to schedule a virtual FM meeting with Myanmar's foreign minister. Min Aung Hlaing excluded from leader-level meetings. Summit also addressed Iran war's impact on ASEAN energy security. Outcome: 'tiny shifts' on Myanmar, no enforcement mechanisms created. Timor-Leste (Myanmar coordination chair) and Thailand sought to build diplomatic momentum. Summit statement reaffirmed Five-Point Consensus. Next key date: scheduled virtual ASEAN-Myanmar FM meeting.

label: Naypyidaw — Myanmar Junta; ASEAN Five-Point Consensus Fails at 5-Year Mark
sub: Myanmar's SAC junta (Min Aung Hlaing, sworn in as president April 2026) offered 100-day peace talks April 21; NUG and all EAOs rejected. SAC ceasefire expired April 30. 48th ASEAN Summit (Cebu, May 5–9) produced only 'tiny shifts' — no enforcement, Five-Point Consensus reaches 5-year anniversary of total non-compliance. May 12: Myanmar junta foreign ministry publicly complained of 'discriminatory measures' and 'pariah treatment' in ASEAN — frustration with post-summit isolation after being excluded from leader meetings. ASEAN SG announced virtual FM meeting 'in the near future' (no date). ASEAN deeply divided: Malaysia/Indonesia/Singapore maintain pressure on atrocity accountability; Thailand/Cambodia/Laos favor re-engagement. Myanmar has 3.3M+ IDPs.
